end.text: Animals that have a backbone are called vertebrates. Animals without a backbone are called invertebrates.
end.sound: Animals that have a backbone are called vertebraytes. Animals without a backbone are called invertebraytes.

end.text: Spiders are invertebrates and are part of the arachnid group. They have eight legs and their body is divided into two parts.
end.sound: Spiders are invertebraytes and are part of the arachnid group. They have eight legs and their body is divided into two parts.

hint.text: The abdomen is the back half of the spider’s body. It contains the spider’s guts, heart, reproductive organs and silk glands.
hint.label: Abdomen

end.text: Snails are invertebrates and are part of the mollusc group. Molluscs are animals which have a soft, unsegmented body and live in aquatic or damp habitats. Many molluscs have a shell to cover their body, but not all do.
end.sound: Snails are invertebraytes and are part of the mollusc group. Molluscs are animals which have a soft, unsegmented body and live in aquatic or damp habitats. Many molluscs have a shell to cover their body, but not all do.

hint.text: The shell protects and supports the soft body of the snail.
hint.label: Shell
